events.title: The American Revolutionary War Begins
events.description: British troops and colonial militia clashed at Lexington and Concord in Massachusetts. The exchanges of gunfire became known as the 'shot heard round the world'.
events.significance: These battles turned growing colonial tension into open armed conflict. They set the colonies on the road to independence and the founding of the United States.

events.title: Charles Darwin Dies
events.description: The British naturalist died at age 73. He is buried in Westminster Abbey.
events.significance: Darwin's theory of evolution by natural selection transformed biology and changed how humanity understands its place in the natural world.

events.title: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising Begins
events.description: When Nazi troops entered the Warsaw Ghetto to deport its remaining Jewish residents, those inside rose up in armed resistance. It was the first mass uprising against German occupation in Poland.
events.significance: Though vastly outgunned, the fighters held out for weeks. The uprising became a lasting symbol of courage and resistance in the face of the Holocaust.

events.title: Salyut 1, the First Space Station, Launches
events.description: The Soviet Union launched Salyut 1, the world's first space station, into Earth orbit.
events.significance: It opened the era of long-duration human spaceflight. It paved the way for later orbital outposts such as Mir and the International Space Station.

events.title: Oklahoma City Bombing
events.description: A truck bomb exploded outside the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City and killed 168 people. Timothy McVeigh, the mastermind of the attack, was later executed.
events.significance: It remains the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history. It led to major changes in American security policy and federal building protection.
